objective: Fix the proven Windows custody close race where native tree termination removes the process before the tracked child exit event is observed, causing a false retryable application-process residue, while preserving identity proof and fail-closed retry behavior; then prove the clean real Tinto stdio journey reaches READY and closes successfully.
closed_decisions: The standard MCP stdio real-Tinto probe now reaches READY and returns bounded surface/snapshot evidence after safe Windows minimum reconstruction.
The same probe's first close returns CLOSE_FAILED with cleanupPending application-process, while the recorded owned PID is absent shortly afterward and its durable lease remains closing.

Tracked custody currently returns retryable immediately when post-termination ownership inspection becomes undefined even though the child exit event may still be pending; a bounded exit wait must decide convergence, not process absence alone.

Never infer safe termination from a missing inspection or PID alone. Successful convergence requires the tracked child exit event or an already-exited tracked child, plus existing postcondition checks in SessionManager.
Do not expand crash recovery, public MCP behavior, environment reconstruction, provider protocol, or release scope.
forbidden_changes: Do not edit files outside the six owned files.
Do not weaken PID, start-time, command-hash, system-hash, nonce, descendant-completeness, listener-owner, custody attachment, or durable-lease checks.

Do not treat missing process inspection as proof of exit, add sleeps without a bounded deadline, broaden termination targets, invoke a shell, or add a second destructive action after ownership proof is lost.

Do not change public MCP tools/schemas/dialog behavior, Windows environment reconstruction, provider/Tinto source, dependencies, manifests, lockfiles, queue/blocker/release files, commits, branches, Jira, or pull requests.

acceptance_criteria.description: When native termination makes custody inspection disappear before the tracked child exit event arrives, termination waits within the existing bounded grace window and returns terminated once the tracked exit event is observed instead of falsely returning retryable.
If the tracked child remains alive or identity/descendant proof is absent before destructive termination, cleanup remains retryable and no unproven or replacement process is terminated.
Focused tracked-process, Windows-process, and SessionManager regression tests cover the post-termination inspection/exit race and fail-closed counterexamples.

The clean real Tinto managed stdio probe reaches READY, returns bounded observation evidence, closes with state idle, and leaves no live owned process or provider listener and no new current-run custody lease.
